entries.sanskrit:
त्रयस् त्रिंशे तु तस्यैव कपिलस्योपदेशतः ।

ज्ञान-भवेन तन्-मातुर् जीवन् मुक्तिर् उदीर्यते ॥

विस्रस्तं मोह-रूपं पटलम् आवरणं यस्याः सा । तत्त्वान्य् एव विषयस् तेनाङ्किता सिद्धिः साङ्ख्य-ज्ञानं तस्य भूमिं क्षेत्रं प्रवर्तकम् ॥१॥
word_for_word: the veil of delusion fallen away
entries.source_note: Pinned source: merged file vishvAsa/purANam_vaiShNavam @ 100560de6c9f68c2875097d40a2012a84c784179; exact chapter marker preserved.
transliteration:
trayas triṃśe tu tasyaiva kapilasyopadeśataḥ |

jñāna-bhavena tan-mātur jīvan muktir udīryate ||

visrastaṃ moha-rūpaṃ paṭalam āvaraṇaṃ yasyāḥ sā | tattvāny eva viṣayas tenāṅkitā siddhiḥ sāṅkhya-jñānaṃ tasya bhūmiṃ kṣetraṃ pravartakam ||1||
entries.literal_english: In the thirty-third chapter, through the instruction of Kapila, his mother’s liberation while living, born of knowledge, is described. Her veil in the form of delusion has fallen away. Her accomplishment is marked by the principles themselves as its object; Sāṅkhya knowledge becomes its field and means of operation.

entries.sanskrit: अथेति वाक्यान्तरे । अजोऽपि तव वपुः केवलं दध्यौ, न तु दृष्टवान् । स च स्वयं साक्षाद् यस्य तव जठराब्जाज् जातः, स भवान् एव विश्वस्य सर्गादि विधत्ते, न तु तव सर्गादि-कर्ता कश्चिद् अस्ति । स एवं-भूतस् त्वं मे मया कथं जठरेण धृत इति त्रयाणाम् अन्वयः । कथं भूतं वपुः ? सत् व्यक्तम् । तत्र हेतुः---अन्तः-सलिले शयानम् । कीदृशम् ? भूतानीन्द्रियाणि चार्थाश् च शब्दादय आत्मा च मन एतन्-मयम् एतैर् व्याप्तम् इत्य् अर्थः । कुतः ? गुणानां प्रवाहो यस्मिंस् तत् । कुतः ? अशेषस्य कार्य-कारणस्य बीजं कारणम् ॥२॥
word_for_word: even the unborn Brahmā merely meditated on Your body
but did not fully see it
born from the lotus of Your abdomen
brings about creation and the rest of the universe
seed of the entire chain of cause and effect
entries.source_note: Pinned source: merged file vishvAsa/purANam_vaiShNavam @ 100560de6c9f68c2875097d40a2012a84c784179; exact chapter marker preserved.
transliteration: atheti vākyāntare | ajo’pi tava vapuḥ kevalaṃ dadhyau, na tu dṛṣṭavān | sa ca svayaṃ sākṣād yasya tava jaṭharābjāj jātaḥ, sa bhavān eva viśvasya sargādi vidhatte, na tu tava sargādi-kartā kaścid asti | sa evaṃ-bhūtas tvaṃ me mayā kathaṃ jaṭhareṇa dhṛta iti trayāṇām anvayaḥ | kathaṃ bhūtaṃ vapuḥ ? sat vyaktam | tatra hetuḥ---antaḥ-salile śayānam | kīdṛśam ? bhūtānīndriyāṇi cārthāś ca śabdādaya ātmā ca mana etan-mayam etair vyāptam ity arthaḥ | kutaḥ ? guṇānāṃ pravāho yasmiṃs tat | kutaḥ ? aśeṣasya kārya-kāraṇasya bījaṃ kāraṇam ||2||
entries.literal_english: Atha introduces another statement. Even the unborn Brahmā merely meditated on Your body; he did not fully see it. Brahmā himself was born directly from the lotus of Your abdomen. You alone bring about the creation and the rest of the universe; no one creates You. How then could such a Lord have been contained in my womb? Your manifest body lies within the cosmic waters and is pervaded by the elements, senses, their objects such as sound, and mind, because the stream of guṇas exists within it and it is the seed-cause of the entire chain of cause and effect.

entries.sanskrit: कथं-भूतो भवान् सर्गादि विधत्ते ? गुण-प्रवाह-रूपेण विभक्तं वीर्यं शक्तिर् येन सः । शक्ति-द्वारेण विधत्ते न साक्षाद् इत्य् अर्थः । यतोऽनीहो निष्क्रियः । तर्हि कथं शक्ति-द्वारेणापि सर्गादि विधत्ते ? तत्राह---अवितथाभिसन्धिः सत्य-सङ्कल्पः । किम्-अर्थं विधत्ते ? आत्मनां जीवानाम् ईश्वरः । जीवानां भोगार्थम् इत्य् अर्थः । ननु कथं विचित्रान् भोगान् एक एव विदध्यात् ? तत्राह---अतर्क्याः सहस्रम् अपरिमिताः शक्तयो यस्य ॥३॥
word_for_word: potency differentiated as the stream of guṇas
for the experience of living beings
entries.source_note: Pinned source: merged file vishvAsa/purANam_vaiShNavam @ 100560de6c9f68c2875097d40a2012a84c784179; exact chapter marker preserved.
transliteration: kathaṃ-bhūto bhavān sargādi vidhatte ? guṇa-pravāha-rūpeṇa vibhaktaṃ vīryaṃ śaktir yena saḥ | śakti-dvāreṇa vidhatte na sākṣād ity arthaḥ | yato’nīho niṣkriyaḥ | tarhi kathaṃ śakti-dvāreṇāpi sargādi vidhatte ? tatrāha---avitathābhisandhiḥ satya-saṅkalpaḥ | kim-arthaṃ vidhatte ? ātmanāṃ jīvānām īśvaraḥ | jīvānāṃ bhogārtham ity arthaḥ | nanu kathaṃ vicitrān bhogān eka eva vidadhyāt ? tatrāha---atarkyāḥ sahasram aparimitāḥ śaktayo yasya ||3||
entries.literal_english: How does the Lord create? His potency is differentiated as the stream of guṇas; He acts through that potency, not directly, for He is inactive. Yet His intention is unfailing, His resolve true. As Lord of the living beings He creates for their experience. Though one, He can produce their diverse experiences because His potencies are inconceivable and innumerable.

entries.sanskrit: किं च, प्रलये यस्योदरे एतद् विश्वम् आसीत् स त्वं मया जठरेण कथं धृतः ? ननु शिशौ मयि किम् एतद् उच्यते ? तत्राह---बट-पत्र इति । अङ्घ्रिं पादाङ्गुष्ठं पिबतीत्य् अङ्घ्रि-पानः । इदम् अपि शिशुत्वं तद्वद् एव मायेति भावः ॥४॥
word_for_word: within whose abdomen the universe rested at dissolution
how were You held in my womb?
entries.source_note: Pinned source: merged file vishvAsa/purANam_vaiShNavam @ 100560de6c9f68c2875097d40a2012a84c784179; exact chapter marker preserved.
transliteration: kiṃ ca, pralaye yasyodare etad viśvam āsīt sa tvaṃ mayā jaṭhareṇa kathaṃ dhṛtaḥ ? nanu śiśau mayi kim etad ucyate ? tatrāha---baṭa-patra iti | aṅghriṃ pādāṅguṣṭhaṃ pibatīty aṅghri-pānaḥ | idam api śiśutvaṃ tadvad eva māyeti bhāvaḥ ||4||
entries.literal_english: How could You, within whose abdomen the universe rested at dissolution, have been contained in my womb? The reference to the banyan leaf recalls the infant Lord sucking His toe; this present childhood too is māyā in just that way.

entries.sanskrit: अथवा न त्वं मयापत्यान्तरम् इव जठरे भृतः, किन्तु वराहाद्य्-अवतार-वद् इच्छयैवाविर्भूतोऽसीत्य् आह---त्वं देह-तन्त्रो देह-परिकरः स्वी-कृत-मूर्तिर् असि । पाप्मनां दुष्टानाम् । निदेश-भाजाम् आज्ञानुवर्तिनां विभूतये समृद्धये । आत्म-पथोपलब्धये ज्ञान-मार्ग-प्रदर्शनाय ॥५॥
word_for_word: not carried like an ordinary child
for revealing the path to the Self
entries.source_note: Pinned source: merged file vishvAsa/purANam_vaiShNavam @ 100560de6c9f68c2875097d40a2012a84c784179; exact chapter marker preserved.
transliteration: athavā na tvaṃ mayāpatyāntaram iva jaṭhare bhṛtaḥ, kintu varāhādy-avatāra-vad icchayaivāvirbhūto’sīty āha---tvaṃ deha-tantro deha-parikaraḥ svī-kṛta-mūrtir asi | pāpmanāṃ duṣṭānām | nideśa-bhājām ājñānuvartināṃ vibhūtaye samṛddhaye | ātma-pathopalabdhaye jñāna-mārga-pradarśanāya ||5||
entries.literal_english: Alternatively, You were not carried in my womb like an ordinary child; like the Varāha and other avatāras, You manifested by Your own will. You have assumed a bodily form: for the destruction of the wicked, for the prosperity of those who obey Your commands, and for revealing the path to realization of the Self.

entries.sanskrit: अतस् त्वद्-दर्शनाद् अहं कृतार्थास्मीति कैमुत्य-न्यायेनाह । यन्-नामधेयस्य श्रवणम् अनुकीर्तनं च तस्मात् । क्वचित् कदाचिद् अपि । श्वानम् अत्तीति श्वादः श्वपचः, सोऽपि सवनाय सोम-यागाय कल्पते योग्यो भवति । अनेन पूज्यत्वं लक्ष्यते ॥६॥
word_for_word: by seeing You I am fulfilled
becomes qualified for the soma sacrifice
entries.source_note: Pinned source: merged file vishvAsa/purANam_vaiShNavam @ 100560de6c9f68c2875097d40a2012a84c784179; exact chapter marker preserved.
transliteration: atas tvad-darśanād ahaṃ kṛtārthāsmīti kaimutya-nyāyenāha | yan-nāmadheyasya śravaṇam anukīrtanaṃ ca tasmāt | kvacit kadācid api | śvānam attīti śvādaḥ śvapacaḥ, so’pi savanāya soma-yāgāya kalpate yogyo bhavati | anena pūjyatvaṃ lakṣyate ||6||
entries.literal_english: Therefore, by seeing You I am fulfilled. By an argument from the greater to the lesser she says that merely hearing and repeating His name is so powerful that even a dog-eater becomes qualified for the soma sacrifice; this indicates that such a person becomes worthy of honor.

entries.sanskrit: तद् उपपादयति---अहो बत आश्चर्ये । यस्य जिह्वाग्रे तव नाम वर्तते सश्वपचोऽप्य् अतोऽस्माद् एव हेतोर् गरीयान् । यद् यस्माद् वर्तते अत इति वा । कुतः ? इत्य् अत आह---त एव तपस् तेपुः कृतवन्तः । जुहुवुर् होमं कृतवन्तः । सस्नुः तीर्थेषु स्नाताः । आर्यास् त एव सदाचाराः। ब्रह्म वेदम् अनूचुर् अधीतवन्तः । त्वन्-नाम-कीर्तने तप-आद्य्-अन्तर्-भूतं, ततस् ते पुण्यतमा इत्य् अर्थः । यद् वा, जन्मान्तरे तैस् तपो-होमादि सर्वं कृतम् इति त्वन्-नाम-कीर्तन-महा-भाग्योदयाद् अवगम्यत इत्य् अर्थः ॥७॥
entries.source_note: Pinned source: merged file vishvAsa/purANam_vaiShNavam @ 100560de6c9f68c2875097d40a2012a84c784179; exact chapter marker preserved.
transliteration: tad upapādayati---aho bata āścarye | yasya jihvāgre tava nāma vartate saśvapaco’py ato’smād eva hetor garīyān | yad yasmād vartate ata iti vā | kutaḥ ? ity ata āha---ta eva tapas tepuḥ kṛtavantaḥ | juhuvur homaṃ kṛtavantaḥ | sasnuḥ tīrtheṣu snātāḥ | āryās ta eva sadācārāḥ| brahma vedam anūcur adhītavantaḥ | tvan-nāma-kīrtane tapa-ādy-antar-bhūtaṃ, tatas te puṇyatamā ity arthaḥ | yad vā, janmāntare tais tapo-homādi sarvaṃ kṛtam iti tvan-nāma-kīrtana-mahā-bhāgyodayād avagamyata ity arthaḥ ||7||
entries.literal_english: She establishes the point: how astonishing! Even a dog-eater on whose tongue-tip Your name is present is for that very reason exalted. Such persons have already performed austerity, offered oblations, bathed at sacred places, lived as noble people, and studied the Veda. Chanting Your name contains within itself the fruit of austerity and the rest; alternatively, the arising of the great fortune of chanting Your name shows that all those practices were performed in a previous birth.

entries.sanskrit: प्रत्यक्-स्रोतसि प्रत्याहृते आत्मनि मनसि संविभाव्यं सञ्चिन्त्यम् । वेदा गर्भे यस्य सः ॥८॥
word_for_word: with the current of the mind turned inward
in the mind withdrawn into the Self
he in whose womb the Vedas reside
entries.literal_english: “Pratyak-srotasi” means with the current of the mind turned inward. It is to be contemplated and carefully considered in the mind withdrawn into the Self. “Veda-garbham” means he in whose womb the Vedas reside.
entries.source_note: Pinned source: merged file vishvAsa/purANam_vaiShNavam @ 100560de6c9f68c2875097d40a2012a84c784179; exact Śrīdhara marker and commentary text preserved.
transliteration: pratyak-srotasi pratyāhṛte ātmani manasi saṃvibhāvyaṃ sañcintyam | vedā garbhe yasya saḥ ||8||

entries.sanskrit: अविक्लवया गम्भीरया वाचा ॥९॥
entries.literal_english: “With an unwavering voice” means with a deep voice.
entries.source_note: Pinned source: merged file vishvAsa/purANam_vaiShNavam @ 100560de6c9f68c2875097d40a2012a84c784179; exact Śrīdhara marker and commentary text preserved.
transliteration: aviklavayā gambhīrayā vācā ||9||

entries.sanskrit: ते तव सु-सेव्येन सुख-सेव्येन मे मयोदितेन । आस्थितेनानुष्ठितेन । परां काष्ठां जीवन्-मुक्तिम् अवरोत्स्यसि प्राप्स्यसि ॥१०॥
entries.source_note: Pinned source: merged file vishvAsa/purANam_vaiShNavam @ 100560de6c9f68c2875097d40a2012a84c784179; exact chapter marker preserved.
transliteration: te tava su-sevyena sukha-sevyena me mayoditena | āsthitenānuṣṭhitena | parāṃ kāṣṭhāṃ jīvan-muktim avarotsyasi prāpsyasi ||10||
entries.literal_english: By the path spoken by Me, easy to follow and well practised, you will attain the supreme limit—liberation while living.

entries.sanskrit: यायाः यास्यसि । अतद्-विदो मन्-मतम् अविद्वांसः ॥११॥
word_for_word: those who do not know that
entries.literal_english: “Yāyāḥ” means “you will attain.” “Those who do not know that” are those who are ignorant of my teaching.
entries.source_note: Pinned source: merged file vishvAsa/purANam_vaiShNavam @ 100560de6c9f68c2875097d40a2012a84c784179; exact Śrīdhara marker and commentary text preserved.
transliteration: yāyāḥ yāsyasi | atad-vido man-matam avidvāṃsaḥ ||11||

entries.sanskrit: अनुमतोऽनुज्ञातः ॥१२॥
entries.source_note: Pinned source: merged file vishvAsa/purANam_vaiShNavam @ 100560de6c9f68c2875097d40a2012a84c784179; exact chapter marker preserved.
transliteration: anumato’nujñātaḥ ||12||
entries.literal_english: Anumata means permitted or given leave.

entries.sanskrit: सरस्वत्या आपीडे पुष्प-मुकुट-तुल्ये । सरस्वत्येति पाठे मुकुटेनेव संवेष्टिते । बिन्दु-सरसि समाहिता बभूव ॥१३॥
word_for_word: at the crown of the Sarasvatī
entries.source_note: Pinned source: merged file vishvAsa/purANam_vaiShNavam @ 100560de6c9f68c2875097d40a2012a84c784179; exact chapter marker preserved.
transliteration: sarasvatyā āpīḍe puṣpa-mukuṭa-tulye | sarasvatyeti pāṭhe mukuṭeneva saṃveṣṭite | bindu-sarasi samāhitā babhūva ||13||
entries.literal_english: At the crown of the Sarasvatī—like a floral crest, or, in another reading, encircled by Sarasvatī like a crown—she became concentrated at Bindu-sarovara.

entries.sanskrit: कथं-भूता सती समाहिता ? तद् आह---अभीक्ष्णं त्रि-सवणम् अवगाहः स्नानं तेन कपिशान् पिशङ्गान् स्वत एव कुटिलानलकान् केशांस् तथात्मानं देहं चीर-धारिणं कृशं च बिभ्रती सती ॥१४॥
entries.source_note: Pinned source: merged file vishvAsa/purANam_vaiShNavam @ 100560de6c9f68c2875097d40a2012a84c784179; exact chapter marker preserved.
transliteration: kathaṃ-bhūtā satī samāhitā ? tad āha---abhīkṣṇaṃ tri-savaṇam avagāhaḥ snānaṃ tena kapiśān piśaṅgān svata eva kuṭilānalakān keśāṃs tathātmānaṃ dehaṃ cīra-dhāriṇaṃ kṛśaṃ ca bibhratī satī ||14||
entries.literal_english: How did she become concentrated? By bathing repeatedly three times daily, her naturally curly locks became tawny; she wore bark garments and her body became lean.

entries.sanskrit: प्रजा-पतेः कर्दमस्य तपो-योगाभ्यां विजृम्भितम् अतिशयितं स्व-गार्हस्थ्यं हित्वा पुत्र-भूतेश्वर-विरहातुरा सती वदनं किञ्चिद् अनिर्वाच्यं शोक-व्याकुलं चकारेति षष्ठेनान्वयः ॥१५॥
word_for_word: distressed by separation from her son, the Lord
entries.source_note: Pinned source: merged file vishvAsa/purANam_vaiShNavam @ 100560de6c9f68c2875097d40a2012a84c784179; exact chapter marker preserved.
transliteration: prajā-pateḥ kardamasya tapo-yogābhyāṃ vijṛmbhitam atiśayitaṃ sva-gārhasthyaṃ hitvā putra-bhūteśvara-virahāturā satī vadanaṃ kiñcid anirvācyaṃ śoka-vyākulaṃ cakāreti ṣaṣṭhenānvayaḥ ||15||
entries.literal_english: Having abandoned the extraordinary household prosperity manifested by Prajāpati Kardama through austerity and yoga, and distressed by separation from her son, the Lord of beings, she made her face somewhat indescribable and overwhelmed with grief.

entries.sanskrit: यत्र गार्हस्थ्ये । क्षीर-फेन-निभा मृदु-शुभ्राः शय्या आस्तरणान्याभान्ति दन्त-घटिता मञ्चकाश् च । स्वर्ण-मयाः परिकराः । आसनानि पीठादीनि । सुस्पर्शान्यास्तरणानि येषु ॥१६॥
word_for_word: soft, white beds like milk foam
entries.literal_english: In that household setting, beds soft and white like milk foam shine, along with ivory-inlaid couches and golden furnishings. There are seats such as benches, with soft-to-the-touch coverings.
entries.source_note: Pinned source: merged file vishvAsa/purANam_vaiShNavam @ 100560de6c9f68c2875097d40a2012a84c784179; exact Śrīdhara marker and commentary text preserved.
transliteration: yatra gārhasthye | kṣīra-phena-nibhā mṛdu-śubhrāḥ śayyā āstaraṇānyābhānti danta-ghaṭitā mañcakāś ca | svarṇa-mayāḥ parikarāḥ | āsanāni pīṭhādīni | susparśānyāstaraṇāni yeṣu ||16||

entries.sanskrit: न कतमेन व्याख्यातम्।
word_for_word: No commentary is given by Śrīdhara here.

entries.sanskrit: बहुभिर् अमर-द्रुमैः रम्यम् ॥१८॥
entries.literal_english: It is beautiful with many celestial trees.
entries.source_note: Pinned source: merged file vishvAsa/purANam_vaiShNavam @ 100560de6c9f68c2875097d40a2012a84c784179; exact Śrīdhara marker and commentary text preserved.

entries.sanskrit: यत्रोद्याने प्रविष्टम् आत्मानं देवहूतिम् ॥१९॥
entries.literal_english: “Where she entered the garden” refers to Devahūti herself.
entries.source_note: Pinned source: merged file vishvAsa/purANam_vaiShNavam @ 100560de6c9f68c2875097d40a2012a84c784179; exact Śrīdhara marker and commentary text preserved.
transliteration: yatrodyāne praviṣṭam ātmānaṃ devahūtim ||19||

entries.sanskrit: आखण्डल इन्द्रस् तस्य या योषितस् तासाम् अपीप्सिततमं प्राप्तुम् इष्टतमं तद् धित्वा तत्राभिमानं त्यक्त्वा ॥२०॥
word_for_word: what they most desired to attain
entries.literal_english: She gave up what was most desired, even among Indra’s wives, and relinquished her identification with it.
entries.source_note: Pinned source: merged file vishvAsa/purANam_vaiShNavam @ 100560de6c9f68c2875097d40a2012a84c784179; exact Śrīdhara marker and commentary text preserved.
transliteration: ākhaṇḍala indras tasya yā yoṣitas tāsām apīpsitatamaṃ prāptum iṣṭatamaṃ tad dhitvā tatrābhimānaṃ tyaktvā ||20||

entries.sanskrit: सुहृद्-वियोगस्य दुःसहताम् आह---वनम् इति । नष्टे वत्से वत्सला गौर् इवाभूत् ॥२१॥
word_for_word: the unbearableness of separation from a beloved
entries.source_note: Pinned source: merged file vishvAsa/purANam_vaiShNavam @ 100560de6c9f68c2875097d40a2012a84c784179; exact chapter marker preserved.
transliteration: suhṛd-viyogasya duḥsahatām āha---vanam iti | naṣṭe vatse vatsalā gaur ivābhūt ||21||
entries.literal_english: He describes how unbearable separation from a beloved is: she became like an affectionate cow whose calf has been lost.

entries.sanskrit: विरह-कृत-ध्यान-फलम् आह---निस्पृहा निर्वासना । वत्स विदुर ।
word_for_word: fruit of meditation produced by separation
entries.source_note: Pinned source: merged file vishvAsa/purANam_vaiShNavam @ 100560de6c9f68c2875097d40a2012a84c784179; exact chapter marker preserved.
transliteration: viraha-kṛta-dhyāna-phalam āha---nispṛhā nirvāsanā | vatsa vidura |
entries.literal_english: He states the fruit of meditation produced by separation. Niḥspṛhā means free from desire or latent craving. “Dear Vidura” addresses the hearer.

entries.sanskrit:
ततः स्व-सुतः कपिलो यद् आह, तद् भगवतो रूपं ध्यायती तद् आत्मानं च विश्वतो-मुखं सर्व-गतं ध्यायती ब्रह्मण्य् अवस्थित-मतिर् बभूवेति पूर्वस्यैवानुषङ्गः । केन ध्यायती ? विशुद्धेनात्मना मनसा ॥२३॥

विशुद्धौ कारणान्य् आह---भक्ति-प्रवाह-रूपेण योगेन वैराग्येण च युक्तानुष्ठानेन जातं यज् ज्ञानं तेन च । युक्तानुष्ठानं च गीता-सूक्तं---

> युक्ताहार-विहारस्य युक्त-चेष्टस्य कर्मसु । >
> युक्त-स्वप्नावबोधस्य योगो भवति दुःख-हा ॥ \[गीता ६.१७\] इति > ।

ब्रह्म-हेतुना ब्रह्मत्वा-पादकेन ॥२४॥

विश्वतो-मुखत्वे हेतुः---स्वानुभूत्या स्वरूप-प्रकाशेन तिरो-भूतम् । माया-गुणैर् विशेषणं परिच्छेदो यस्य ॥२५॥

कथं-भूते ब्रह्मणि ? आत्मनां जीवानां संश्रये भगवति ॥२६॥
word_for_word: through yoga as a continuous flow of devotion
and through the knowledge born from them
in Bhagavān, refuge of living beings
entries.source_note: Pinned source: merged file vishvAsa/purANam_vaiShNavam @ 100560de6c9f68c2875097d40a2012a84c784179; exact chapter marker preserved.
transliteration:
tataḥ sva-sutaḥ kapilo yad āha, tad bhagavato rūpaṃ dhyāyatī tad ātmānaṃ ca viśvato-mukhaṃ sarva-gataṃ dhyāyatī brahmaṇy avasthita-matir babhūveti pūrvasyaivānuṣaṅgaḥ | kena dhyāyatī ? viśuddhenātmanā manasā ||23||

viśuddhau kāraṇāny āha---bhakti-pravāha-rūpeṇa yogena vairāgyeṇa ca yuktānuṣṭhānena jātaṃ yaj jñānaṃ tena ca | yuktānuṣṭhānaṃ ca gītā-sūktaṃ---

> yuktāhāra-vihārasya yukta-ceṣṭasya karmasu | >
> yukta-svapnāvabodhasya yogo bhavati duḥkha-hā || \[gītā 6.17\] iti > |

brahma-hetunā brahmatvā-pādakena ||24||

viśvato-mukhatve hetuḥ---svānubhūtyā svarūpa-prakāśena tiro-bhūtam | māyā-guṇair viśeṣaṇaṃ paricchedo yasya ||25||

kathaṃ-bhūte brahmaṇi ? ātmanāṃ jīvānāṃ saṃśraye bhagavati ||26||
entries.literal_english: Meditating on the form of Bhagavān as taught by her own son Kapila, and on the Self as all-faced and all-pervading, she became established in Brahman with purified mind. Purity arose through knowledge born from the combined practice of the continuous flow of devotion and detachment. Properly regulated practice is the discipline praised in the Gītā. Brahman itself is the cause that establishes Brahmanhood. By direct realization the limiting distinctions imposed by māyā’s guṇas disappeared, because the Brahman meditated upon is Bhagavān, the refuge of all living beings.

entries.sanskrit: ननु तथापि गुणानां विद्यमानत्वात् कथम् अस्मरणम् ?तत्राह---नित्यारूढो लब्ध-प्रतिष्ठः समाधिर् यस्यास् तस्या भावस् तत्त्वं तस्मात् । परावृत्तः शान्तो गुण-निमित्तो भ्रमो यस्याः सा ।
entries.source_note: Pinned source: merged file vishvAsa/purANam_vaiShNavam @ 100560de6c9f68c2875097d40a2012a84c784179; exact chapter marker preserved.
transliteration: nanu tathāpi guṇānāṃ vidyamānatvāt katham asmaraṇam ?tatrāha---nityārūḍho labdha-pratiṣṭhaḥ samādhir yasyās tasyā bhāvas tattvaṃ tasmāt | parāvṛttaḥ śānto guṇa-nimitto bhramo yasyāḥ sā |
entries.literal_english: How could the guṇas be forgotten while they still existed? Because her samādhi was permanently established; through that reality the delusion caused by the guṇas had turned away and become pacified.

entries.sanskrit: परतः परभिर् एव कर्दम-सृष्ट-विद्याधरीभिः पोषः पोषणं यस्य । आधिर् मनो-ग्लानिस् तद् असंभवाद् अकृशः मलैर् अवच्छन्नोऽपि बभौ ।
word_for_word: not emaciated because it was absent
though covered with impurities, it shone
entries.source_note: Pinned source: merged file vishvAsa/purANam_vaiShNavam @ 100560de6c9f68c2875097d40a2012a84c784179; exact chapter marker preserved.
transliteration: parataḥ parabhir eva kardama-sṛṣṭa-vidyādharībhiḥ poṣaḥ poṣaṇaṃ yasya | ādhir mano-glānis tad asaṃbhavād akṛśaḥ malair avacchanno’pi babhau |
entries.literal_english: Her body was nourished by others, namely the Vidyādharī attendants created by Kardama. Because mental distress was absent it did not become emaciated; though covered with impurities, it still shone.

entries.sanskrit: दैव-गुप्तम् आरब्ध-कर्म-पालितम् ॥२९॥
entries.source_note: Pinned source: merged file vishvAsa/purANam_vaiShNavam @ 100560de6c9f68c2875097d40a2012a84c784179; exact chapter marker preserved.
transliteration: daiva-guptam ārabdha-karma-pālitam ||29||
entries.literal_english: “Protected by destiny” means sustained by the karma already begun to fructify.

entries.sanskrit: निर्वाणं नित्यम् उक्तम् ॥३०॥
entries.source_note: Pinned source: merged file vishvAsa/purANam_vaiShNavam @ 100560de6c9f68c2875097d40a2012a84c784179; exact chapter marker preserved.
transliteration: nirvāṇaṃ nityam uktam ||30||
entries.literal_english: Nirvāṇa is described as eternal.

entries.sanskrit: हे वीर विदुर ! उपेयुषी प्राप्ता ॥३१॥
entries.literal_english: “O hero, Vidura!” “Upayyuṣī” means “having attained.”
entries.source_note: Pinned source: merged file vishvAsa/purANam_vaiShNavam @ 100560de6c9f68c2875097d40a2012a84c784179; exact Śrīdhara marker and commentary text preserved.
transliteration: he vīra vidura ! upeyuṣī prāptā ||31||

entries.sanskrit: हे सौम्य, तस्यास् तन् मर्त्यं शरीरं सरिद् अभूत् । कथं-भूतम् ? योगेन विधूता विलीना मार्त्या दैहिका धातु-मला यस्य ॥३२॥
word_for_word: the mortal body became a river
entries.source_note: Pinned source: merged file vishvAsa/purANam_vaiShNavam @ 100560de6c9f68c2875097d40a2012a84c784179; exact chapter marker preserved.
transliteration: he saumya, tasyās tan martyaṃ śarīraṃ sarid abhūt | kathaṃ-bhūtam ? yogena vidhūtā vilīnā mārtyā daihikā dhātu-malā yasya ||32||
entries.literal_english: O gentle one, her mortal body became a river. Its mortal bodily constituents and impurities had been dissolved and shaken off through yoga.

entries.sanskrit: कपिलोऽपि ययाव् इत्य् उक्तं तद् एव प्रपञ्चयति, कपिलोऽपीति त्रिभिः । समनुज्ञाप्यानुज्ञां संप्रार्थ्य ॥३३॥
entries.source_note: Pinned source: merged file vishvAsa/purANam_vaiShNavam @ 100560de6c9f68c2875097d40a2012a84c784179; exact chapter marker preserved.
transliteration: kapilo’pi yayāv ity uktaṃ tad eva prapañcayati, kapilo’pīti tribhiḥ | samanujñāpyānujñāṃ saṃprārthya ||33||
entries.literal_english: The text had said that Kapila also departed; he now expands this in three verses. Samanujñāpya means having requested permission and taken leave.

entries.sanskrit: दत्तम् अर्हणम् अर्ध्यं निकेतनं च यस्मै ॥३४॥
word_for_word: and a place to dwell was given to him
entries.literal_english: He was offered respectful hospitality, an arghya water offering, and a place to stay.
entries.source_note: Pinned source: merged file vishvAsa/purANam_vaiShNavam @ 100560de6c9f68c2875097d40a2012a84c784179; exact Śrīdhara marker and commentary text preserved.
transliteration: dattam arhaṇam ardhyaṃ niketanaṃ ca yasmai ||34||

entries.sanskrit: उपशान्त्य् अर्हं समाहित आस्ते ॥३५॥
entries.literal_english: He remains seated, absorbed and fit for tranquility.
entries.source_note: Pinned source: merged file vishvAsa/purANam_vaiShNavam @ 100560de6c9f68c2875097d40a2012a84c784179; exact Śrīdhara marker and commentary text preserved.
transliteration: upaśānty arhaṃ samāhita āste ||35||

entries.sanskrit: प्रकरणार्थम् उपसंहरति---एतद् इति । तव त्वया ॥३६॥
word_for_word: he concludes the point of the chapter
entries.literal_english: He concludes the point of the chapter with “etat” (“this”); “tava” is glossed as “by you.”
entries.source_note: Pinned source: merged file vishvAsa/purANam_vaiShNavam @ 100560de6c9f68c2875097d40a2012a84c784179; exact Śrīdhara marker and commentary text preserved.
transliteration: prakaraṇārtham upasaṃharati---etad iti | tava tvayā ||36||

entries.sanskrit: एतच् छ्रवण-कीर्तन-फलम् आह---य इति । सुपर्ण-केतौ गरुड-ध्वजे । उपलभते प्राप्नोति ॥३७॥
word_for_word: the Lord with Garuḍa on His standard
entries.source_note: Pinned source: merged file vishvAsa/purANam_vaiShNavam @ 100560de6c9f68c2875097d40a2012a84c784179; exact chapter marker preserved.
transliteration: etac chravaṇa-kīrtana-phalam āha---ya iti | suparṇa-ketau garuḍa-dhvaje | upalabhate prāpnoti ||37||
entries.literal_english: He states the fruit of hearing and chanting this account. “He whose banner bears Suparṇa” means the Lord with Garuḍa on His standard. Upalabhate means one attains Him.
